key_insight: FlashAttention-4 co-designs the attention algorithm with kernel-level pipelining tuned for Blackwell-class GPUs (B200/GB200), matching asymmetric compute/memory scaling to recover throughput and reduce stalls compared to Hopper-optimized kernels.
problem_solved: Existing attention kernels (e.g., FlashAttention-3) were tuned for Hopper (H100) and suffer degraded performance on Blackwell systems that exhibit asymmetric hardware scaling (compute vs. memory/tensor-core behavior), limiting throughput, latency, and long-context capability.
method: Asymmetric-aware tiling and double-buffered pipelining: partition attention into stages and overlap memory movement with compute tailored to per-SM resources.
Warp-role specialization and phase scheduling: assign warps to distinct pipeline stages to avoid global synchronization and reduce stalls on heterogenous hardware units.
Kernel co-design and autotuning: fuse/reorder sub-operations, shrink peak memory footprint, and autotune tile sizes and pipeline depth to Blackwell L1/L2 and tensor-core characteristics.
impact: Delivers higher sustained attention throughput and lower latency on Blackwell GPUs, enabling larger context windows and lower cost-per-token for LLM inference/training without changing model architecture.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic of H100 vs Blackwell resource asymmetry (compute vs memory/cache) with callouts.
Pipeline timeline comparing non-pipelined vs FlashAttention-4 pipelined kernel showing overlapped load/compute/store stages.
Bar chart of throughput and latency across architectures (H100, B200, GB200) and kernel versions (baseline, FlashAttention-3, FlashAttention-4).
Heatmap or block diagram showing tile/warp assignment and utilization across SMs to illustrate reduced stalls and improved utilization.
paper_title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
paper_authors: Ted Zadouri, Markus Hoehnerbach, Jay Shah, Timmy Liu, Vijay Thakkar
